 2   Q.   What does this section of your testimony discuss?

 3   A.   This section of my testimony deals with the issue of affordability and how

 4        it should be considered in the context of this case. Although New Mexico

 5        statutes and Commission rules do not define affordability explicitly, the

 6        Commission has historically recognized the importance of ensuring rates

 7        are affordable for customers, promoting rate stability, and applying the

 8        principle of gradualism when necessary to avoid abrupt and dramatic

 9        customer bill impacts.

10

11   Q.   How would EPE’s as-filed proposal in this case impact revenue

12        requirements for the Company’s various rate classes?

13   A.   EPE presents a total revenue requirement of $210.8 million that results from

14        a requested $70.5 million net revenue requirement increase. The

15        Company’s proposal would result in significant increases to the revenue

16        requirement for the majority of EPE’s rate classes and produce associated

17        substantial bill impacts for those customers. Table CED-2, below, shows

18        that 6 of the 14 rate classes would have class revenue requirement increases

 6   Q.   Is it important to define the concepts of affordability and rate shock

 7        with strict meanings in order for the Commission to consider those

 8        factors when making a determination in this case?

 9   A.   No, Staff does not believe that terms like affordability or rate shock must

10        be strictly defined for the Commission to take those factors into

11        consideration in this case. In particular, the concept of affordability may not

12        lend itself to a strict definition with limits and ranges that can be rigorously

13        and uniformly applied across cases because what constitutes “affordable”

14        may be different from one customer to the next, or from one time period to

15        another. As noted by the Commission in a recent case, determining

16        affordability is an activity that is inherently fact-specific and time

 4   Q.      Has the Commission previously made decisions that support customer

 5           affordability and help mitigate rate shock for customers?

 6   A.      Yes. Ensuring affordability and protecting customers from rate shock are

 7           longstanding considerations of the Commission. The Commission regularly

 8           evaluates the effects of proposed rate increases on customers and issues

 9           decisions designed to mitigate rate shock. One approach used by the

10           Commission is to apply gradualism rather than adhering to strict

11           applications of class cost of service when determining appropriate rates. For

12           example, in El Paso Electric Company’s most recent general rate case

13           before this Commission, Case No. 20-00104-UT, the Commission’s June

14           23, 2021 Order adopted the Recommended Decision of the Hearing
